;Armed conflicts and attacks
*[[War in Afghanistan (2001–present)|War in Afghanistan]]
**A [[2 and 5 September 2019 Kabul bombings|car bomb explodes]] in [[Kabul]], killing 16 people and wounding over 100 others. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2019/09/suicide-car-bomb-attack-rocks-eastern-kabul-190902180659647.html (Al Jazeera)]
**A [[suicide bomber]] attacks a police station in [[Kunduz]], [[Afghanistan]]. At least six police officers are killed and another seventeen wounded. [http://www.xinhuanet.com/english/2019-09/02/c_138359315.htm (Xinhua)]
**Six Afghan army soldiers were killed and three police officers wounded after Taliban militants ambushed their patrol in the country's eastern Ghazni province. [http://www.xinhuanet.com/english/2019-09/02/c_138358133.htm (Xinhua)]
*Gunmen open fire on a vehicle carrying [[Colombia|Colombian]] mayoral candidate Karina García, killing her, her mother, a candidate for the municipal council, and three activists. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-colombia-violence/colombian-mayoral-candidate-killed-government-blames-rebel-dissidents-idUSKCN1VN26F?il=0 (Reuters)]
*A [[Tunisian National Guard]] officer and three fighters from an armed group are killed in a security operation in the region of [[Kasserine Governorate|Kasserine]], [[Tunisia]]. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2019/09/tunisia-security-boss-fighters-killed-clash-border-190902094037292.html (Al Jazeera)]
;Disasters and accidents
*[[Sinking of MV Conception|Sinking of MV ''Conception'']]
**The [[United States Coast Guard]] says that 25 people died, nine went missing and five crew members have been rescued after a fire on a diving boat near [[Santa Cruz Island]], off the coast of [[California]]. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-us-canada-49556638 (BBC News)]
*[[2019 Atlantic hurricane season]]
**After killing at least five people in [[the Bahamas]], [[Hurricane Dorian]] is downgraded to a [[Saffir–Simpson scale|Category Four hurricane]] as it approaches the [[southeastern United States]]. [https://www.nytimes.com/2019/09/02/us/hurricane-dorian-updates.html (''The New York Times'')] [https://www.msnbc.com/msnbc/watch/hurricane-dorian-downgrades-to-a-category-4-storm-but-remains-powerful-68027461715 (MSNBC)]

;Law and crime
*[[2019 Papua protests]]
**Amid an ongoing [[Internet blackout]] across [[Western New Guinea|Papua]], [[Indonesia]] says [[Municipal Police (Indonesia)|police]] have banned "[[fake news]]", "violent demonstrations" and "carrying out or spreading [[separatism]] in expressing opinions in public". The [[Chief of the Indonesian National Police]] announces that the security detail in the region has been reinforced with 6,000 troops. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-indonesia-papua/indonesian-police-ban-violent-protests-separatism-in-papua-idUSKCN1VN0DQ (Reuters)]
*[[Corruption in Spain]]
**Close to 40 people, including former presidents of [[Community of Madrid]] and senior politicians [[Esperanza Aguirre]], [[Ignacio González González|Ignacio González]] and [[Cristina Cifuentes]], are charged by the [[Audiencia Nacional]] with alleged crimes during the instruction of the Púnica corruption case. [https://www.elmundo.es/madrid/2019/09/02/5d6d1158fc6c83c1718b45bb.html (''El Mundo'')]
*A court in [[Russia]] orders the seizure of the 41.6% share of equity in [[Vostochny Bank]] controlled by [[private equity]] firm [[Baring Vostok Capital Partners|Baring Vostok]]. The seizure, requested by Vostochny itself, is the latest move in continuing litigation over alleged embezzlement by Baring Vostok executives. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-russia-business-detention/russian-court-orders-seizure-of-stake-in-bank-in-dispute-with-baring-vostok-idUSKCN1VN0NO (Reuters)] [http://www.rapsinews.com/judicial_news/20190902/303462666.html (RAPSI)]
*Former [[Member of Parliament (United Kingdom)|British MP]] [[Nigel Waterson]]'s son, 26-year-old Stephen Waterson, admits to having killed 3-year-old Alfie Lamb in 2018 by crushing him to death in the footwell of a vehicle. [https://metro.co.uk/2019/09/02/ex-ministers-son-admits-crushing-boy-3-death-car-seat-10672204/ (''Metro'')]
*[[Italy|Italian]] police seize a migrant rescue boat after it spent over a week stranded at sea unable to find a port to accept it; over 100 migrants begin to disembark in [[Sicily]]. [https://www.euronews.com/2019/09/02/migrants-disembark-from-german-rescue-ship-seized-in-italy (euronews)]
*A ship carrying 635 mostly [[Afghanistan|Afghan]] migrants from the crowded refugee camp on the [[Greece|Greek]] island of [[Lesbos]] arrives in the mainland port city of [[Thessaloniki]]. A second ship carrying 800 more is expected to arrive tomorrow. They are to be housed in {{ill|Nea Kavala|el|Νέα Καβάλα Κιλκίς}}, where a camp already houses 1,000 migrants. [https://www.boston25news.com/news/the-latest-31-migrants-taken-off-italian-ngo-rescue-ship/981782721 (Boston 25 News)]
*A 40-year-old man allegedly kills eight children outside a [[primary school]] in [[Hubei]], [[China]]. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-asia-china-49563337 (BBC News)]
*Former Guatemalan presidential candidate [[Sandra Torres]] is arrested for possible charges of illegal financing in her election campaign in 2015. She was given preventive detention at the Mariscal Zavala Military Center. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-latin-america-49551036 (BBC News)]

;Politics and elections
*[[Government of Georgia (country)|Government of Georgia]], [[Bakhtadze government]]
**[[Prime Minister of Georgia|Georgian Prime Minister]] [[Mamuka Bakhtadze]] announces his [[resignation]] on [[Facebook]]. [https://www.arabnews.com/node/1548626/world (AFP via ''Arab News'')]
*[[Brexit]]
**[[Prime Minister of the United Kingdom|UK Prime Minister]] [[Boris Johnson]] holds discussions about a possible [[snap election]] in the face of opposition to leaving the [[European Union]] without a deal. Those against Johnson's plan to leave in late October with or without a deal within his own [[Conservative Party (UK)|Conservative Party]] are warned they may be expelled from the party. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/uk-politics-49549960 (BBC News)]
